historical_basis: Moss people (Moosleute), also wood folk (Holzleute) or forest folk (Waldleute), are a class of fairy-folk compared with dwarfs, elves or spirits, described in German folklore as intimately tied to trees and the forest. Moss people are sometimes like dwarfs, child-sized but grey, old-looking, hairy and moss-clad; sometimes bigger, and in other accounts pretty. Moss people, especially females, can send plagues yet also heal their victims; in epidemics the Holzfräulein came out of the forest to show which herbs cure or prevent plague. Moosweiblein live in the forest, on heaths, in dark places or the deepest woods; they dwell in earth holes, hollow trees, root huts or moss huts, sleep on moss and bed their children on moss or bark.
